subtitle: Every classifier you'll ever build is estimating a conditional probability.

code:
print(pd.crosstab(df.plan, df.churned, margins=True))
#          0    1   All
# Free    350  150   500
# Paid    450   50   500

caption: Overall P(churn) = 0.2 -- but that hides what's happening inside each plan.

eyebrow: P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B)
code:
print(df.groupby("plan")["churned"].mean())
# Free    0.3
# Paid    0.1

# check: P(Free and churn)=0.15, P(Free)=0.5 -> 0.15/0.5 = 0.3
caption: Conditioning is just filtering, then taking a mean -- exactly what groupby already does.

eyebrow: The multiplication rule: P(A and B) = P(B) x P(A|B)
code:
# two cards, no replacement, both aces:
(4/52) * (3/51)   # ~0.004525  -- correct
(4/52) ** 2       # ~0.0059    -- WRONG: ignores the first draw
caption: The second draw is conditional -- once one ace is gone, only 3 of 51 cards remain aces.

eyebrow: Independence: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
code:
d = rng.integers(1, 7, size=(1_000_000, 2))
A, B = d[:,0] == 6, d[:,1] >= 4
print(A.mean(), B.mean())    # 0.1665  0.5003
print((A & B).mean())        # 0.0831
print(A.mean() * B.mean())   # 0.0833  -- near match = independence
caption: Plan and churn are NOT independent (0.3 != 0.2); two dice ARE, within simulation noise.
